title: Narravity HEX payload-rack: answer 4 technical follow-up questions (interface/CAD/transport)
description:
Narravity (Hideyuki "Hide" Nakanishi) sent 4 technical follow-up questions on 7/17 after the 7/13 site visit, re: interfacing their HEX standardized payload-rack system to the BLK3 bulkhead. John tagged this to Phil (@exobot assigned to Phil). CC: kei@, mike@, kuge@, cherish@ (Narravity); Neil Milburn, Lizi Quinn, Russell Blink (Exos).

QUESTIONS TO ANSWER:
1. Custom bulkhead cost range (e.g. to relocate the power/data interface location).
2. Interface loads/stress between bulkhead and HEX system - requests CAD model or drawing of the bulkhead for reference (PUG drawing lacks wall thickness between mounting holes and depth of the hollow section).
3. Transport of the integrated payload module on the trailer:
   a. Transported by itself or connected to other vehicle structures/modules?
   b. How is the module secured on the trailer?
   c. Any shock absorbers / vibration isolation, given ~25G was mentioned?
   d. Typical orientation during transport (bulkhead up, or laid sideways)?

EXO PRE-WORK (attached response scaffold):
- Framing/process answers drafted (integration at Exos, module handling, offer CAD under existing confidentiality, 2-day turnaround).
- PLACEHOLDERS needing Phil/engineering data: custom-bulkhead price range (Q1); bulkhead CAD/drawing export - Neil Milburn / Russell Blink (Q2); transport rigging/orientation specifics (Q3, Phil's ops domain).
- INTERNAL FLAG for Phil: the ~25G Narravity cites (Q3c) does not match the BLK3 Payload User's Guide flight envelope (boost <4g; max transient shock ~7g at touchdown). Confirm whether 25G is a road-transport/handling shock limit vs a flight number before answering, so we don't publish an inconsistent figure.

title: Email notification on task assignment — auto-notify assignee when a Mission Control task is assigned
description:
**Owner:** [ASSIGN:Phil Eaton]
**Assigned by:** Phil Eaton (7/17) via @Exobot email command.
**Status:** 🟡 Requested — build the notifier.

**Request (Phil):** Set up an email notification system so that when someone is assigned a Mission Control task, that person automatically receives an email letting them know a new task was assigned to them.

**Why it's feasible now:** The Supabase `tasks` table already carries `assigned_email`, `assigned_to`, and `assigned_at` on every row. A watcher can diff newly-assigned tasks and email the assignee — no schema change needed.

**Proposed implementation (for Phil to approve):**
1. New script `scripts/task-assignment-notifier.py` — polls Supabase `tasks` for rows where `assigned_email` is set and the assignment is new/changed since last run (track a seen-state file keyed on task id + assigned_email + assigned_at, same pattern as the priority-inbox / decision-send watchers).
2. On a new assignment, send an email via ProtonMail Bridge/msmtp to the assignee: subject "New Mission Control task assigned to you: <title>", body with title, description snippet, due date, board link (localhost:8080). CC/notify Jon optional.
3. Schedule via launchd (e.g. every 10 min), wrapped in task_ledger.py, and register with the cron failure watchdog.
4. Guardrails: only notify on assignments to real Exos addresses; dedupe so re-runs never double-send; skip if assigned_email == the person who created it (self-assign) if desired.

**Next step:** Phil approves the approach (or tweaks cadence / who gets CC'd), then Exo builds + schedules it.

title: International Trade Zone @ Spaceport America - inbound foreign-payload fly-&-return (decision-driven)
description:
OBJECTIVE: Establish an inbound International Trade Zone at Spaceport America (NM) to host incoming foreign-country payloads and fly-and-return them, using existing law only (no new regime). Domestic/inbound mirror of the Japan/HOSPO "container-as-zone" outbound package.

LEGAL STACK: (1) Customs = Foreign-Trade Zone via Alternative Site Framework usage-driven site under a county grantee (Dona Ana FTZ #197 = live template; NOTE the launch complex sits in Sierra County, no FTZ grant, so a pad site needs a Sierra grant or an FTZ-Board subzone). (2) Per-payload temporary admission = TIB (HTSUS Ch.98/9813, re-export <=1yr, extendable to 3) or ATA Carnet (bond-free) for fly-and-return. (3) Export control = reuse USML IV(a) suborbital lane + EAR 9x515/EAR99 + License Exception CSA + one program TAA. (4) Return leg = FAA Part 450 launch + reentry/recovery. Partners: NM Spaceport Authority + county FTZ grantee + customs broker.

STEP LADDER:
1. Greenlight + framing (Exo drafts 1-page domestic concept; confirm launch-site county).
2. FTZ path selection (A: extend Dona Ana FTZ #197 service area/subzone; B: Sierra County FTZ grant; C: FTZ-Board subzone at pad).
3. NM Spaceport Authority partnership outreach (they own the spaceport = natural co-applicant).
4. CBP port director + FTZ Board feasibility inquiry.
5. Payload temp-admission SOP: TIB default + ATA Carnet for ally customers; customs-broker shortlist.
6. Export-control: fold inbound question into the existing DDTC advisory request (vs separate CJ).
7. FAA AST Part 450 reentry/recovery pre-application question.
8. NM federal/state engagement map (NM Spaceport Authority, Dona Ana FTZ board, Sens. Heinrich/Lujan, Rep. Vasquez).
9. Assemble full inbound package + identify first foreign pilot customer/country; approve filing/outreach sequence.

DONE WHEN: FTZ site designation path is filed and a pilot foreign-payload fly-and-return is structured under TIB/Carnet with export-control + FAA coverage in place.

title: Industrial Base capture — DIB Consortium (OTA) + IBAS for domestic composite cryo-tank/COPV + GTL-machined-RDRE production (decision-driven)
description:
OBJECTIVE: Win non-dilutive funding to stand up / expand DOMESTIC production of Exos's hard-part capability — Type-5 linerless composite cryo tanks & COPVs (Scorpius/Torrance), Integrated Pressurized Structures, reusable-launch components, and the owned GTL-machined RDRE path — via the LOWER-BARRIER industrial-base vehicles that move faster than a full DPA Title III.

VEHICLES: (1) Defense Industrial Base Consortium (DIBC) — an OTA-based consortium that releases Requests for Project Proposals (RPPs); membership is the gate to see/bid; faster + lower-barrier than FAR. (2) IBAS (Industrial Base Analysis & Sustainment, OSD Industrial Base Policy / MCEIP) — funds projects that close defense industrial-base shortfalls, often executed through the DIBC OTA. DPA Title III = the larger/slower follow-on once a shortfall + demand signal are proven.

THE SHORTFALL EXOS CLOSES: domestic capacity for linerless Type-5 composite cryogenic tankage / COPVs and reusable-launch composite structures (most COPV/cryo-tank capacity is thin or foreign-exposed), plus a domestic GTL-machined RDRE production path. Frame with the physical-AI / re-industrialization thesis ("AI for atoms; domestic production of the hard parts").

STRATEGY LINK: same capability as the RDRE flight-demo capture — the RDRE flight demo (NASA Phase III + TACFI) proves the GTL-machined engine; DIBC/IBAS funds the production line. Non-dilutive; complements Series A.

HOW THIS MOVES (decision-driven, daily): exactly ONE open decision sits in /decisions at a time. Each time Jon answers it, Exo executes that step and opens the next.

STEP LADDER:
1. Greenlight + framing (Exo drafts 1-page industrial-base concept = the shortfall Exos closes; confirm DIBC manager + Exos membership path).
2. DIBC membership (confirm administrator/NSTXL; authorize membership application if not already a member — the gate to RPPs).
3. Lock the primary shortfall narrative (Type-5 composite cryo-tank/COPV capacity vs reusable-launch components vs RDRE GTL machining) against a real IBAS/DPAS gap.
4. POC / sponsor: find the OSD Industrial Base Policy (MCEIP/IBAS) or Service office that owns the shortfall + the DIBC RPP pipeline; warm path.
5. Government demand signal: identify/secure a Service or prime that needs the capacity (Space Force/MDA/launch prime) — IBAS/Title III require demand.
6. Vehicle selection: DIBC OTA project proposal vs direct IBAS agreement vs stage DPA Title III later.
7. Draft the DIBC RPP response / IBAS white paper (capacity expansion, cost share, schedule).
8. Teaming + cost share (Scorpius/Torrance line, AI-native manufacturing); finalize.
9. Submit through the consortium (routes through Jon for gov).

DONE WHEN: a DIBC RPP response / IBAS project proposal is submitted against a defined shortfall with a government demand signal and cost-share in place.

title: Send reply to Daniel Murphy (NOAA CSL) — SACSS / AIRL whitepaper
description:
Ready-to-send delivered to Jon's inbox 2026-07-21 09:47.

TO: daniel.m.murphy@noaa.gov
CC: Gregory.J.Frost@noaa.gov; victoria.breeze@noaa.gov
SUBJECT: RE: ESA document on atmospheric impacts of reentry

Hello Daniel,

Thank you for sending the AIRL whitepaper, it is exactly the framing we have been working toward. The finding that spaceflight is now the dominant stratospheric source of aluminium, copper, and lead, paired with how little in-situ data exists above the aircraft ceiling, lines up directly with the capability we have been developing at Exos.

We have been designing SACSS, a suborbital sampling system on our FAA-licensed, reusable BLK3 vehicle that opens and seals collection chambers across three altitude bands from roughly 40 to 100 km, on both ascent and descent, and returns intact physical samples for laboratory composition work. It is meant to be the in-situ, physical-sample-return leg of exactly the kind of measurement campaign the whitepaper calls for.

A few questions where your read would be valuable:
- On the U.S. side, who is scoping the measurement-campaign funding the whitepaper recommends, and is there a natural place for a physical-sampling platform in that plan?
- Would it be useful for us to walk you and the team through the SACSS concept and the composition data it would return?

Best regards,
John Quinn
Cofounder and CEO, Exos Aerospace
